chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Artie Shaw's new band: Lena Horne record and Lips Page arrangements
summary: Shaw's lawyer called him to write for the new band; they made a Lena Horne record and he arranged Blues in the Night before Shaw joined the Navy.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: : Then Shaw made his big hit and then he went to Mexico, right, and when he came back --
When he came back, there was --
It would have to be around the forties, somewhere around there.

He was putting together a new band. His lawyer called me up. What was his name? Andy Weinberg. He called up and he said, "Artie's getting this band together, and he would like you to give him a call." So we got together, we went down and made a record before we got the band together, we went down and made a record with Lena Horne.
For Victor. I think it came out. At least I got it on tape up there. They guy -- had to get it from some guy. Vince Giordano, I think, gave it to me.
Well, let's see that didn't last too long because he went in the Army -- he went in the Navy.
: But you did some things that Lips Page sang on, with Artie.

With Artie. "Blues in the Night," Take Your Shoes Off, Baby. Several other things. Johnny Guarnieri was in the band then. Georgie Auld. Les Robinson. Fine lead player. Jack Jenney, and his wife sang. She sang This Time The Dream's On Me-" That was recorded.
